title: Inspiration
definition: Inspiration is the work of God by which the Holy Spirit moved upon the writers of Scripture so that what was written is truly the Word of God.
summary: The doctrine of inspiration teaches that Scripture is not merely human reflection about God, but God-breathed truth given through human authors. The Bible carries divine authority because its source is God Himself. Inspiration does not erase the personality or historical setting of the writers, but it means that the Spirit of God superintended the writing of Scripture so that it faithfully communicates God’s truth.

studySections.heading: God-Breathed Scripture
studySections.content: Second Timothy 3:16 says that all Scripture is breathed out by God. This means Scripture has its origin in God, not merely in man. Because God is true, His Word is trustworthy and profitable for teaching, reproof, correction, and training in righteousness.

studySections.heading: The Holy Spirit and the Human Writers
studySections.content: Second Peter 1:20-21 teaches that prophecy did not originate from man’s will, but men spoke from God as they were carried along by the Holy Spirit. Inspiration includes both divine authority and real human authorship.

studySections.heading: Purpose of Inspired Scripture
studySections.content: God gave inspired Scripture so that His people may know Him, be corrected by Him, be equipped for good works, and be led to salvation through faith in Jesus Christ. The goal is not mere knowledge, but a life surrendered to Christ and shaped by the Spirit.
